newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to buy Dracula choppers despite NATO snub.
newsitem.headline: Romania to buy Dracula choppers despite NATO snub.

text.p: Romania will go ahead with a deal to buy NATO-compatible helicopters, reportedly financed with help from Merrill Lynch, despite Washington's decision to leave Bucharest out of first NATO enlargement.
"The programme will go ahead as planned, no matter if Romania joins NATO in the first wave or not," Constantin Dudu Ionescu, State Secretary at the Defence Ministry, told Reuters.

Last month the ministry said it would buy 96 AH-1RO Dracula helicopters to be co-produced by a venture between Romania's Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) aircraft maker and U.S. firm Bell Helicopter Textron.

The helicopter deal, estimated at $1.5 billion and the biggest project in post-communist Romania, is part of the country's efforts to align its military equipment to NATO standards. The Dracula aircrat is derived from the AH-1W Supercobra used by the U.S. Marine Corps.

On Thursday Washington dampened Romania's hopes of getting NATO entry soon, by naming the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary as its choices for the alliance's first eastward expansion, to be announced at a Madrid summit next month.
U.S. officials said Washington's decision was final, but Romanian leaders have vowed to push on with their country's bid.
"Of course, we still have to solve problems related to the financial part of the helicopter deal," Ionescu said.
Local media quoted Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea as saying that U.S. investment bank Merril Lynch would help finance the deal, which should not punch a hole in Romania's budget.
On Friday, a senior Merrill Lynch executive declined to comment.

Under the deal, the first helicopter should be delivered within two years. The new aircraft's General Electric engines would be built under license by Romania's Turbomecanica SA aircraft engine maker.
Local military sources told Reuters recently avionics for the 96 Draculas would be supplied by Israel's Elbit Ltd.

The sources also said Romania planned to launch a programme to buy 100 advanced jet fighters. Among aircraft that would be considered are Lockheed Martin's F-16, McDonnell Douglas' F-18, Mirage 2000-5 by France's Dassault and the multi-national Eurofighter 2000.
Romania spends annually about $800 million on defence.
